objectives:
In the course, students will expect to:

	Develop a critical understanding of literary texts produced under the reign of Elizabeth I

	Develop the historical/political mindset to interrogate the representations of Elizabeth I in the context of early modern queenship

	To cultivate and enhance the skill set of research and project-making via both
in-class activities and take-home assignment
content:
*本課程為英文系中高年級專業文學課程，並以全英文授課。非此設定範圍但欲選修該課程的同學(含本系及外系同學)，請務必參與開學第一堂課，並在課後與授課老師集體短暫面談。若符合修課標準，會視情況核發選課密碼卡。若有其他問題，請直接來信授課老師。If you need the passcode, you MUST attend the first meeting.

For centuries Elizabeth I has attracted much attention from historians via several distinct public images: she is the disavowed daughter of Henry VIII and the ‘great whore’ Anne Boleyn, the loving sister of Edward VI, the religious rivals of Mary Tudor and Mary of Scots, and of course, the virgin Queen, and literatures converging on these images have testified to the golden age of England in the sixteenth century, from Philip Sidney to John Lyly, from William Shakespeare to Edmund Spenser. How do we come to terms with Elizabeth’s omnipresence in literature (particularly as a female ruler)? What does it say about the interplay between literature and politics in the Renaissance? In what way can we think of the queen as a major influencer of sixteenth-century England? With these core questions in mind, this course seeks to read a cluster of important literary texts centering on the political representation of Elizabeth I. The entire course will be taught in English and is suitable for those who are interested in the history, culture, and literature of the early modern period. Former knowledge in English Studies 1 is preferred but not required.

數個世紀以來，英國女皇伊莉莎白一世一直是歷史學家熱切關注的對象；她的形象多元而富有爭議：她是亨利八世與「大淫婦」安妮・博林的女兒、是愛弟如命的姊姊、是瑪麗・都鐸與瑪麗・斯圖雅特這兩位宗教政敵的對手、更是鼎鼎大名的童貞女王。而圍繞這些形象所形成的文學作品—從菲利普・席德尼、約翰・萊利、到莎士比亞與史賓賽—共同見證了英國十六世紀的黃金時代。站在現代的角度，我們該如何理解伊莉莎白在文學作品中的各種鏡像呢？這些現象如何揭示文學與文藝復興時期政治之間的互動關係？我們又可以從哪些面向思考她身為十六世紀英格蘭最重要的媒體影響者？本課程將以這些核心問題為出發點，細讀一系列聚焦於伊莉莎白一世政治形象的文學作品。本課程全程以英文授課，適合對早期現代時期的歷史、文化與文學有興趣的學生選修。有修過英文學一或莎士比亞相關課程者尤佳，但非必須條件。
books:
There will be NO physical course reader. All of our course readings (primary and secondary) will be provided by the instructor after the first day of class via google document (in pdf files). Students can determine if they want to have the texts printed out; however, whatever they choose, students MUST have the text while in class: either you carry the print-out, or you bring the laptop/ electronic reader (your phone does not count). No text, no attendance.

	John Foxe, excerpts from Book of Martyrs (1563)
	Selections of Petrarchan Sonnets
	John Lyly, Endymion (1588)
	William Shakespeare, A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595)
	Thomas Dekker, The Whore of Babylon (1607)
